flawed_step: Step 5: uniqueness of the minimum cut does not imply that the difference of two maximum flows must vanish; distinct flows may differ by an internal circulation.
counterexample: Let the other two vertices be u and v. Take arcs s→u of capacity 1, u→t of capacity 2, u→v of capacity 1, and v→u of capacity 1, with no other arcs. The unique minimum cut is {s}, but for every x∈[0,1], the flow f(s→u)=f(u→t)=1 and f(u→v)=f(v→u)=x is a maximum flow. Thus x=0 and x=1 give distinct maximum flows.
assessment_summary:
1. [JUSTIFIED] Label the two vertices other than s and t by u and v; every s-t cut is then one of {s}, {s,u}, {s,v}, and {s,u,v}.
2. [JUSTIFIED] To attempt a proof, suppose f and g are two maximum flows. Their difference d=f−g satisfies flow conservation at u and v, and its net s-t value is zero because f and g have the same value.
3. [JUSTIFIED] Therefore, proving d=0 on every arc would prove f=g and establish uniqueness of the maximum flow.
4. [JUSTIFIED] A nonzero d can represent a circulation: flow may be increased around a directed cycle without changing its s-t value or violating conservation, provided residual capacity is available.
5. [NOT JUSTIFIED] One might claim that uniqueness of the minimum cut rules out every such nonzero circulation. This does not follow: cut capacities constrain s-t throughput, while a circulation wholly among intermediate vertices need not affect any flow value. This is the first failure of the attempted proof.
6. [NOT JUSTIFIED] The proposed conclusion d=0, and hence f=g, cannot be obtained from Step 5.
7. [JUSTIFIED] Consider instead the four-vertex network with arcs s→u of capacity 1, u→t of capacity 2, u→v of capacity 1, and v→u of capacity 1, and no other arcs. It satisfies all stated network conditions.
8. [JUSTIFIED] The capacities of the four cuts {s}, {s,u}, {s,v}, and {s,u,v} are respectively 1, 3, 2, and 2.
9. [JUSTIFIED] Hence {s} is the network's unique minimum s-t cut, with capacity 1.
10. [JUSTIFIED] For each x∈[0,1], define f_x(s→u)=1, f_x(u→t)=1, and f_x(u→v)=f_x(v→u)=x.
11. [JUSTIFIED] Each f_x respects all capacities and conservation: at u both total inflow and outflow are 1+x, and at v both are x.
12. [JUSTIFIED] Each f_x has value 1. No flow can have value greater than 1 because the cut {s} has capacity 1, so every f_x is maximum.
13. [JUSTIFIED] The maximum flows f_0 and f_1 are distinct because they differ on u→v and v→u.
14. [JUSTIFIED] Thus this network has exactly one minimum cut but more than one maximum flow, so the statement is false.
